title: Tomato Cultivation, Fertilizer Regimen & Early/Late Blight Management
source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru
content: Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) thrives in well-drained loamy soil with pH 6.0 to 7.0. Nursery preparation: Raise seedlings in pro-trays with sterilized coco-peat @ 100-125 g/ha under 50% shade net to prevent Tomato Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV) transmitted by whitefly. Seedlings are ready for transplanting in 25-30 days (height 10-15 cm). Spacing: 90 cm x 60 cm for indeterminate varieties and 60 cm x 45 cm for determinate hybrids. Provide bamboo staking or trellising for indeterminate hybrids at 30 DAT. Irrigation: Drip irrigation with fertigation is strongly recommended; drip saves 40% water and increases yield by 30%. Critical stages: Flowering and fruit enlargement. Disease control: Early Blight (Alternaria solani) causes concentric target-board brown spots on lower leaves. Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans) causes water-soaked necrotic lesions. Management: Spray Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5 g/litre or Chlorothalonil 75 WP @ 2 g/litre prophylactically. If disease appears, spray Azoxystrobin 23 SC @ 1 ml/litre or Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2 g/litre. Precaution: Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation which splashes fungal spores onto foliage.
